chapterTitle: Children of God and Love in Deed and Truth
themeTitle: “See How Great a Love the Father Has Given to Us”

scripture.text: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.
scripture.understanding: ἴδετε ποταπὴν ἀγάπην δέδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ πατήρ, “See how great a love the Father has given to us” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family): ‘Look!’; ποταπός, of what sort, from what country: a love so foreign to this world it astonishes; ἀγάπη, from the love family. ἵνα τέκνα θεοῦ κληθῶμεν, “that we should be called children of God!” — τέκνον, from the children family: children by birth, not merely by adoption of name. Many manuscripts add ‘and we are’. διὰ τοῦτο ὁ κόσμος οὐ γινώσκει ἡμᾶς, ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτόν, “For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him” — κόσμος, from the world family; γινώσκω, from the know family.

scripture.text: Beloved, now we are children of God, and it is not yet revealed what we will be. But we know that, when he is revealed, we will be like him; for we will see him just as he is.
scripture.understanding: ἀγαπητοί, νῦν τέκνα θεοῦ ἐσμεν, “Beloved, now we are children of God” — ἀγαπητός, from the love family; τέκνον, from the children family: the present is certain. καὶ οὔπω ἐφανερώθη τί ἐσόμεθα, “and it is not yet revealed what we will be” — φανερόω, from the appear family: made visible; the future is not yet visible. οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐὰν φανερωθῇ, ὅμοιοι αὐτῷ ἐσόμεθα, “But we know that, when he is revealed, we will be like him” — οἶδα, from the know family and the see family: settled knowledge; ὅμοιος, alike. ὅτι ὀψόμεθα αὐτὸν καθώς ἐστιν, “for we will see him just as he is” — ὁράω, also from the see family. Seeing Him will transform us (2 Corinthians 3:18).

scripture.text: Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.
scripture.understanding: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἔχων τὴν ἐλπίδα ταύτην ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ, “Everyone who has this hope set on him” — ἐλπίς, the confident expectation of seeing Christ. ἁγνίζει ἑαυτὸν καθὼς ἐκεῖνος ἁγνός ἐστιν, “purifies himself, even as he is pure” — ἁγνίζω, to make clean, the word of James 4:8 and 1 Peter 1:22; ἁγνός, pure. Hope is not passive; it is purifying.

scripture.text: Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.
scripture.understanding: πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιεῖ, “Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness” — two words from the sin family: ἁμαρτία, missing the mark, and ἀνομία, lawlessness, rebellion against God's law. καὶ ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία, “Sin is lawlessness.” — not a small slip but defiance; the false teachers may have treated sin as unimportant. ‘Lawlessness’ also recalls the ‘man of lawlessness’ of the last days (2 Thessalonians 2:3).

scripture.text: You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and in him is no sin.
scripture.understanding: καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ἐφανερώθη ἵνα τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἄρῃ, “You know that he was revealed to take away our sins” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family); φανερόω, from the appear family: His first coming; αἴρω, to lift and carry away, the word of John 1:29; ἁμαρτία, from the sin family. καὶ ἁμαρτία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν, “and in him is no sin” — the sinless One came to remove sin. To persist in sin is to oppose the purpose of His coming.

scripture.text: Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him.
scripture.understanding: πᾶς ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ μένων οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει, “Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin” — μένω, to remain; ἁμαρτάνω, from the sin family, in the present tense: does not keep on sinning as a settled way of life. John has already said that believers do sin and must confess (1:8–2:1); here he describes the direction of a life. πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρτάνων οὐχ ἑώρακεν αὐτὸν οὐδὲ ἔγνωκεν αὐτόν, “Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him” — ὁράω, from the see family; γινώσκω, from the know family.

scripture.text: Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.
scripture.understanding: τεκνία, μηδεὶς πλανάτω ὑμᾶς, “Little children, let no one lead you astray” — τεκνίον, from the children family; πλανάω, the deceiving of 2:26. ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην δίκαιός ἐστιν, “He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous” — the false teachers apparently said you could be righteous without doing righteousness. John says practice reveals nature.

scripture.text: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil.
scripture.understanding: ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν, “He who sins is of the devil” — ἁμαρτία, from the sin family; διάβολος, the slanderer. ὅτι ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ὁ διάβολος ἁμαρτάνει, “for the devil has been sinning from the beginning” — ἁμαρτάνω, from the sin family, present tense: continuous. εἰς τοῦτο ἐφανερώθη ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, “To this end the Son of God was revealed” — φανερόω, from the appear family. ἵνα λύσῃ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, “that he might destroy the works of the devil” — λύω, to loose, to undo, to dismantle; ἔργον, from the work family. Jesus came to take apart everything the devil has built.

scripture.text: Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him; and he can’t sin, because he is born of God.
scripture.understanding: πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἁμαρτίαν οὐ ποιεῖ, “Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin” — γεννάω, from the birth family: perfect tense, has been born and remains so; ἁμαρτία, from the sin family. ὅτι σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει, “because his seed remains in him” — σπέρμα, seed: God's own life, implanted by the Spirit and the word (1 Peter 1:23). καὶ οὐ δύναται ἁμαρτάνειν, “and he can’t sin” — δύναμαι, from the power family: is not able. Read with 1:8–10, this means that a child of God cannot go on sinning as a settled way of life, because God's nature in him resists it; it does not teach sinless perfection.

scripture.text: In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil. Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother.
scripture.understanding: ἐν τούτῳ φανερά ἐστιν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ διαβόλου, “In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil” — φανερός, from the appear family: plain, out in the open; τέκνον, from the children family: family likeness shows. “Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother.” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family. Two marks: righteousness and love.

scripture.text: For this is the message which you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another;
scripture.understanding: ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγγελία ἣν ἠκούσατε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, “For this is the message which you heard from the beginning” — ἀγγελία, the message, as in 1:5. ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, “that we should love one another” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family. The gospel always included love.

scripture.text: unlike Cain, who was of the evil one, and killed his brother. Why did he kill him? Because his deeds were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
scripture.understanding: οὐ καθὼς Κάϊν ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἦν, “unlike Cain, who was of the evil one” — πονηρός, from the evil family: actively harmful, ‘the evil one’, the devil. καὶ ἔσφαξεν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, “and killed his brother” — σφάζω, to slaughter, to butcher. “Why did he kill him? Because his deeds were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” — ἔργον, from the work family; πονηρός again. Cain hated Abel not for any wrong Abel did but because Abel's goodness exposed his evil.

scripture.text: Don’t be surprised, my brothers, if the world hates you.
scripture.understanding: μὴ θαυμάζετε, ἀδελφοί, “Don’t be surprised, my brothers” — θαυμάζω, to marvel. εἰ μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος, “if the world hates you” — μισέω; κόσμος, from the world family. The Cain spirit is still alive; Jesus said, ‘If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you’ (John 15:18).

scripture.text: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.
scripture.understanding: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι μεταβεβήκαμεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν, “We know that we have passed out of death into life” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family); μεταβαίνω, to move house, to cross over, the word Jesus used in John 5:24; θάνατος, death; ζωή, from the life family: the life of God. ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τοὺς ἀδελφούς, “because we love the brothers” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family: love is the evidence, not the cause, of new life. “He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.”

scripture.text: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
scripture.understanding: πᾶς ὁ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἀνθρωποκτόνος ἐστίν, “Whoever hates his brother is a murderer” — ἀνθρωποκτόνος, a man-killer, the word Jesus used of the devil (John 8:44). Hatred is murder in the heart, as Jesus taught (Matthew 5:21–22). καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι πᾶς ἀνθρωποκτόνος οὐκ ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἐν αὐτῷ μένουσαν, “and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family); ζωή, from the life family; αἰώνιος, from the time family.

scripture.text: By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
scripture.understanding: ἐν τούτῳ ἐγνώκαμεν τὴν ἀγάπην, “By this we know love” — γινώσκω, from the know family; ἀγάπη, from the love family. ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἔθηκεν, “because he laid down his life for us” — ψυχή, from the life family: His own self, His natural life, as distinct from ζωή (v. 14), the divine life He gives; τίθημι, to lay down, the shepherd's word (John 10:11). καὶ ἡμεῖς ὀφείλομεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν τὰς ψυχὰς θεῖναι, “And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers” — ὀφείλω, to owe: the cross is not only our salvation but our pattern. The John 3:16 of love in action.

scripture.text: But whoever has the world’s goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?
scripture.understanding: ὃς δ᾽ ἂν ἔχῃ τὸν βίον τοῦ κόσμου, “But whoever has the world’s goods” — βίος, the third word of the life family in this passage: the means of living, possessions, as distinct from ζωή (v. 14) and ψυχή (v. 16); κόσμος, from the world family. καὶ θεωρῇ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχοντα, “and sees his brother in need” — θεωρέω, from the see family: to look at, to observe at length; χρεία, need. καὶ κλείσῃ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, “and closes his heart of compassion against him” — κλείω, to shut a door; σπλάγχνα, from the mercy family: the inner parts, where compassion is felt. “how does God’s love remain in him?” — ἀγάπη, from the love family. If you will not give your βίος, how can you claim you would give your ψυχή?

scripture.text: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
scripture.understanding: τεκνία μου, “My little children” — τεκνίον, from the children family. μὴ ἀγαπῶμεν λόγῳ μηδὲ τῇ γλώσσῃ, “let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family; λόγος, from the word family, here mere talk; γλῶσσα, the tongue of James 3. ἀλλὰ ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, “but in deed and truth” — ἔργον, from the work family: the same truth James taught (James 2:15–16).

scripture.text: And by this we know that we are of the truth, and persuade our hearts before him,
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γνωσόμεθα ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐσμέν, “And by this we know that we are of the truth” — γινώσκω, from the know family: love in action is evidence of belonging to the truth. καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πείσομεν τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν, “and persuade our hearts before him” — πείθω, to persuade, to reassure, to calm. A troubled conscience can be quieted by the evidence of real love.

scripture.text: because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.
scripture.understanding: ὅτι ἐὰν καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν ἡ καρδία, “because if our heart condemns us” — καταγινώσκω, to know against, to accuse: a close relative of γινώσκω from the know family. ὅτι μείζων ἐστὶν ὁ θεὸς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν, “God is greater than our heart” — our conscience is not the final judge. καὶ γινώσκει πάντα, “and knows all things” — γινώσκω, from the know family: He knows our sins, but He also knows our love for Him, His Son's sacrifice and His own work in us (John 21:17).

scripture.text: Beloved, if our hearts don’t condemn us, we have boldness toward God;
scripture.understanding: ἀγαπητοί, “Beloved” — from the love family. ἐὰν ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν μὴ καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν, “if our hearts don’t condemn us” — not because we are sinless, but because we are walking in the light and confessing. παρρησίαν ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεόν, “we have boldness toward God” — παρρησία, the confidence of 2:28, now in prayer.

scripture.text: and whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτῶμεν λαμβάνομεν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, “and whatever we ask, we receive from him” — αἰτέω, from the pray family: to ask as a child asks a father; λαμβάνω, to receive. ὅτι τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηροῦμεν, “because we keep his commandments” — τηρέω, from the hold family. καὶ τὰ ἀρεστὰ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ποιοῦμεν, “and do the things that are pleasing in his sight” — ἀρεστός, pleasing. Obedience does not earn answers, but it aligns our asking with His will (5:14).

scripture.text: This is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he commanded.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ, “This is his commandment” — singular: one command with two parts. ἵνα πιστεύσωμεν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, “that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ” — the first mention of faith in the letter, the test of truth. καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, “and love one another” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family, the test of love. καθὼς ἔδωκεν ἐντολὴν ἡμῖν, “even as he commanded” — ἐντέλλομαι. Faith and love are one command.

scripture.text: He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him. By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ τηρῶν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν αὐτῷ, “He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him” — τηρέω, from the hold family; μένω both ways: mutual indwelling, as Jesus said (John 15:4). καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι μένει ἐν ἡμῖν, ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος οὗ ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν, “By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us” — γινώσκω, from the know family; πνεῦμα, the Holy Spirit, the first mention in the letter: the inner witness of the anointing (2:20, 27) and of Romans 8:16.

visualMeditations.title: Called Children
visualMeditations.image: Picture an orphan standing in a courtroom, ragged and frightened. The judge reads the adoption order, and a man steps forward, kneels, and says, ‘This is my child.’ He gives the child his name, his home and his inheritance. Years later the child, grown, looks into a mirror and sees, more and more, the face of the father who claimed him.
visualMeditations.meaning: “See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God!” (v. 1). “Beloved, now we are children of God, and it is not yet revealed what we will be. But we know that, when he is revealed, we will be like him; for we will see him just as he is” (v. 2). You are already God's child; one day you will fully bear His likeness.

visualMeditations.title: Two Families
visualMeditations.image: Picture two families at a reunion. In one, everyone shares the same kind eyes and warm laugh; in the other, the same cold stare and sharp tongue. You can tell which family a stranger belongs to just by watching how they behave.
visualMeditations.meaning: “In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil. Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother” (v. 10). The family likeness shows. Christ came to destroy the works of the devil (v. 8), and His seed in you produces His likeness: righteousness and love.

visualMeditations.title: The Shepherd's Life Laid Down
visualMeditations.image: Picture a shepherd on a hillside at night, wolves circling the flock. He steps between the sheep and the wolves, armed only with a staff, knowing he may not walk away. In the morning the flock is safe, and the shepherd lies still among them.
visualMeditations.meaning: “By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers” (v. 16). The cross defines love. Most of us will not be asked to die for another believer, but we are asked every day to lay down our time, comfort, money and rights for them.

visualMeditations.title: The Closed Door
visualMeditations.image: Picture a comfortable house on a cold night. Through the window you can see a warm fire and a full table. Outside, a fellow believer knocks, shivering and hungry. Inside, someone glances at the door, recognises the face, and quietly turns the key in the lock.
visualMeditations.meaning: “But whoever has the world’s goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?” (v. 17). “My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth” (v. 18). Love is proved at the door, not in the prayer meeting.

structure.label: Children of God (v. 1-3)
structure.body: See the Father's great love: we are called and truly are God's children; the world does not know us because it did not know Him; what we will be is not yet revealed, but when He appears we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is; this hope purifies.

structure.label: Sin and the Son's Mission (v. 4-10)
structure.body: Sin is lawlessness; Christ appeared to take away sins and in Him is no sin; whoever remains in Him does not go on sinning; whoever practises sin is of the devil, whose works the Son came to destroy; whoever is born of God cannot keep on sinning, because God's seed remains in him; righteousness and love reveal the children of God.

structure.label: Love Versus Hatred (v. 11-18)
structure.body: The message from the beginning is to love one another, unlike Cain who murdered his brother; do not be surprised if the world hates you; love shows we have passed from death to life, while hatred is murder; Christ laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for each other; closing our hearts to a brother in need shows God's love is absent; love must be in deed and truth.

structure.label: Assurance Before God (v. 19-24)
structure.body: Loving in deed reassures our hearts before God, who is greater than our hearts and knows all things; if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence in prayer and receive what we ask, because we obey; His command is to believe in His Son and love one another; whoever obeys remains in Him, and we know He remains in us by the Spirit He has given.

sections.heading: What Love the Father Has Given
paragraphs: John breaks out in wonder: “See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God!” (v. 1). The word ποταπός suggests a love from another country — utterly unlike anything in this world. God does not merely tolerate us or employ us; He makes us His children. And it is not just a title: “now we are children of God” (v. 2). The world does not recognise this, just as it did not recognise Jesus.

But the best is still to come: “it is not yet revealed what we will be. But we know that, when he is revealed, we will be like him; for we will see him just as he is” (v. 2). Paul says the same: “For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son” (Romans 8:29), and “When Christ, our life, is revealed, then you will also be revealed with him in glory” (Colossians 3:4). Seeing Christ will complete the transformation that has already begun.

That hope changes how we live now: “Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure” (v. 3). Jesus said, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God” (Matthew 5:8). If you expect to see Him, you prepare to look like Him.

sections.heading: Can a Christian Sin?
paragraphs: Verses 4–10 contain some of the most puzzling statements in the letter. “Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin” (v. 6). “Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him; and he can’t sin, because he is born of God” (v. 9). Yet John has already said, “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves” (1:8), and “If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father” (2:1). How do these fit together?

The strongest answer lies in the Greek present tense, which describes ongoing, habitual action. John is not saying that a believer never commits an act of sin, but that a child of God cannot settle into sin as a way of life — cannot practise it without grief, confession and change. The reason is God's ‘seed’: His life planted in the believer, which fights against sin from within. Paul asks, “Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?” (Romans 6:1) and answers, “May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?” (Romans 6:2). The false teachers apparently said sin did not matter; John says it matters supremely, because it is lawlessness (v. 4), it is the devil's work (v. 8), and Christ came to take it away (v. 5).

So the test is direction, not perfection. “To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil” (v. 8). A person who is comfortable in sin, who defends it and makes no fight against it, shows the family likeness of the devil, who ‘has been sinning from the beginning’. A person who grieves over sin, confesses it and keeps turning towards righteousness and love shows the likeness of the Father (v. 10).

sections.heading: Love in Deed and Truth
paragraphs: The message from the beginning is “that we should love one another” (v. 11). John's negative example is Cain, who killed his brother “Because his deeds were evil, and his brother’s righteous” (v. 12). Hatred of goodness is the devil's own spirit. So believers should not be surprised when the world hates them (v. 13). Hebrews says Abel, “being dead, still speaks” (Hebrews 11:4).

Love is the evidence of new life: “We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers” (v. 14). Jesus used the same words: “he who hears my word, and believes him who sent me, has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life” (John 5:24). Hatred, by contrast, is murder in seed form (v. 15), as Jesus taught in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:21–22).

Then John defines love by the cross: “By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers” (v. 16). And he brings it down to earth: “But whoever has the world’s goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?” (v. 17). Notice the three Greek words for life in verses 14–17: ζωή, the eternal life we have received; ψυχή, the self Christ laid down; βίος, the possessions we are asked to share. If we will not share our βίος, our claim to be willing to give our ψυχή is empty. “My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth” (v. 18). James said the same: words of blessing without bread help no one (James 2:15–16).

sections.heading: When Our Hearts Condemn Us
paragraphs: Tender consciences can be troubled by such high standards. John speaks to them: “And by this we know that we are of the truth, and persuade our hearts before him, because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things” (vv. 19–20). Real acts of love are evidence that we belong to the truth. And when our conscience still accuses us, we appeal to a higher court: God knows everything — our sin, yes, but also our faith in His Son, our love for His people and His own work in us. Peter, grieved, said to Jesus, ‘Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you’ (John 21:17).

When our hearts are at rest, “we have boldness toward God; and whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments” (vv. 21–22). Jesus promised, “All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive” (Matthew 21:22). Obedience does not buy answers; it brings our desires into line with God's.

John then sums up the whole letter in one command with two parts: “that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another” (v. 23). Faith and love belong together. And the final assurance is the Spirit: “By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us” (v. 24). Paul says, “The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God” (Romans 8:16).

ntConnection.heading: Children, the Destroyer of the Devil's Works, and the Good Shepherd
paragraphs: Verse 8 is one of the great mission statements of Christ: He was revealed “that he might destroy the works of the devil.” Hebrews describes how: “that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil” (Hebrews 2:14). Jesus described the devil in the same terms John uses: “He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him” (John 8:44).

Verse 16 echoes Jesus' own words: “Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends” (John 15:13), and “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep” (John 10:11). The same verb, τίθημι, ‘lay down’, is used in each place. John watched the Good Shepherd do it.

The transformation of verse 2 is described by Paul: “But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit” (2 Corinthians 3:18). And the assurance of verse 20 — God greater than our hearts — finds its fullest expression in Romans: “There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:1).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort”. The word grew from an older form that asked ‘from what land?’ — used of something foreign and astonishing. John uses it of the Father's love: a love from another world, unlike anything human. Its gift is that we are called τέκνα θεοῦ, children of God, from the children family — family by birth, not just by name. The world cannot understand this love, because it never understood the Son who revealed it.

Strong's: “illegality, i.e. violation of law”. ἀνομία is from the sin family, meaning ‘without law’: living as if God's law did not exist. John defines sin itself as lawlessness, refusing any view of sin as merely a weakness or an illness. Jesus will say to false prophets, ‘Depart from me, you who work ἀνομία’ (Matthew 7:23). Every sin, however small it seems, is a declaration of independence from God.

Strong's: “something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant”. σπέρμα is God's life implanted in the believer — the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4), the incorruptible seed of the word (1 Peter 1:23), the Spirit Himself. Because this seed remains, the believer cannot comfortably settle into sin. Like produces like: those born (γεννάω, from the birth family) of God bear His likeness.

lexicon.strongs: G979 (life ζωή, zōḗ, G2222; life ψυχή, psychḗ, G5590)
lexicon.insight: Strong's: “life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood.” Verses 14–17 use all three words from the life family. ζωή (v. 14) is the divine life believers receive; ψυχή (v. 16) is the natural self, which Christ laid down; βίος (v. 17) is the means of life — money, food, possessions. The argument is from greater to lesser: if Christ gave His ψυχή, and we have received ζωή, how can we refuse to share our βίος?

Strong's: “to note against, i.e. find fault with.” καταγινώσκω is γινώσκω (to know) with κατά (against): a knowledge that accuses. Our heart ‘knows against’ us. But God, who also γινώσκει πάντα, ‘knows all things’, is greater. Conscience is a real witness, but not the final judge. For a believer walking in the light, God's knowledge of the cross and of His own work in us overrules our self-condemnation.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit wants you to see the Father's love, take sin seriously, and love your brothers and sisters in costly, practical ways.

items.title: Look at the Father's Love
items.body: “See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God!” (v. 1). Do you see yourself as God's child, or only as His servant or His project? The Spirit wants you to stop and look at His love. Spend time today simply receiving it, and let it change how you see yourself.

items.title: Is There a Sin You Are Comfortable With?
items.body: John says that a child of God cannot settle into sin as a way of life. Is there a sin you have stopped fighting, excused or made peace with? The Spirit is not condemning you; He is reminding you that the Son of God came “that he might destroy the works of the devil” (v. 8). Ask Him to destroy that work in you.

items.title: Whose Need Have You Seen?
items.body: “But whoever has the world’s goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?” (v. 17). The Spirit brings someone to mind — a believer in material, emotional or practical need. What part of your βίος — your money, time, home or skills — is He asking you to share this week?

audit.title: The Identity Check
audit.body: Do you live as a child of God, secure in the Father's love, or as an orphan who must earn approval (vv. 1–2)?

audit.title: The Purity Check
audit.body: Does your hope of seeing Christ make you purify yourself (v. 3)? Is there a pattern of sin you have stopped resisting (vv. 6–9)?

audit.title: The Deed Check
audit.body: When did your love last cost you something in money, time or comfort (vv. 16–18)? Is there a brother or sister in need to whom you have closed your heart?

practices.title: Lay Down Something This Week
practices.body: Choose one concrete way to ‘lay down your life’ for a fellow believer this week (v. 16): give money to meet a need, spend an evening helping someone move or repair something, visit someone lonely, or give up something you wanted so another can have it. Do it quietly, in deed and truth.

practices.title: Answer a Condemning Heart
practices.body: When your conscience accuses you after you have confessed, read verses 19–20 aloud. Write down evidence of God's work in you — faith in His Son, love for His people, desire to obey. Then pray, ‘Lord, You are greater than my heart, and You know all things.’ Rest in His verdict.

prayerReflection: “Father, see how great a love You have given me, that I should be called Your child — and that is what I am. Thank You that one day, when Christ appears, I will be like Him, for I will see Him as He is. Let that hope purify me now. I confess that sin is lawlessness, and I do not want to make peace with any of it. Thank You that Jesus was revealed to take away my sins and to destroy the works of the devil. Let Your seed in me grow, so that I bear Your family likeness in righteousness and love. Thank You that I have passed from death into life. Teach me love as Jesus showed it, laying down His life for me, and make me willing to lay down my life — my time, my comfort, my goods — for my brothers and sisters. Never let me close my heart to someone in need. Let my love be in deed and truth, not only in words. When my heart condemns me, remind me that You are greater than my heart and know all things. Give me confidence in prayer as I keep Your commands, believe in the name of Your Son and love one another. Thank You for the Spirit You have given me, by whom I know You remain in me. In Jesus' name, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Cain and Abel
storyConnections.summary: Cain and Abel both brought offerings to God. God accepted Abel's but not Cain's. Instead of turning to God, Cain grew angry, and God warned him that sin was crouching at the door, desiring to have him. Cain did not master it. He lured his brother into the field and killed him. When God asked, ‘Where is Abel your brother?’ Cain answered, ‘Am I my brother's keeper?’ John says Cain hated Abel because Abel's deeds were righteous and his own were evil. Hatred, envy and murder are the family likeness of the evil one; love is the likeness of God.

storyConnections.title: The Good Samaritan
storyConnections.summary: A man was beaten by robbers and left half dead on the road. A priest saw him and passed by on the other side; so did a Levite. Then a Samaritan — a despised outsider — saw him, was moved with compassion, bandaged his wounds, put him on his own animal, took him to an inn and paid for his care. Jesus asked who proved to be a neighbour, and said, ‘Go and do likewise.’ The priest and Levite closed their hearts; the Samaritan opened his heart and his purse. That is the difference between love in word and love in deed.

storyConnections.title: Peter: ‘Lord, You Know Everything’
storyConnections.summary: After Peter's denial, the risen Jesus asked him three times, ‘Do you love me?’ The third time, Peter was grieved, perhaps feeling the weight of his three denials. His answer appealed to Jesus' greater knowledge: “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you” (John 21:17). His own heart could condemn him, but Jesus knew the truth about his love. John was there. He writes that when our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts and knows all things.
